ai.literal: Without embracing, do not remain, feign anger; the distressful pain he experiences, let us see a little.
ai.translation: Do not embrace him immediately; feign a little anger instead, so that we may watch for a moment the painful distress he suffers.
ai.modern: அவரைத் தழுவாமல் உடனே ஏற்றுக்கொள்ளாமல் சற்றே ஊடுவாயாக; அதனால் அவர் அடையும் துன்ப நோயை நாம் சிறிது நேரம் காண்போம்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine (or her companion addressing her) speaks of the sweet play of feigned anger in love. Instead of immediately embracing the returning lover, she decides to hold back and feign a lovers' tiff. The key words 'allal nōy' (distressful pain) and 'kāṇkam' (let us see) show that this feigned anger is not out of malice, but a playful test to enjoy seeing how much the lover longs for her embrace. By delaying the union, she intensifies the pleasure of their eventual reunion.

ai.literal: Feigned anger is like salt in right measure; allowing that to prolong is like being a little excessive.
ai.translation: Feigned anger in love is like salt in food; it is delightful in the right measure, but to prolong it is like adding a little too much.
ai.modern: ஊடல் கொள்வது உணவில் உப்பு அளவாக இருப்பதற்கு ஒப்பானது; ஆனால் அந்த ஊடலை நீட்டிக்கச் செய்வது உப்பு சற்றே அதிகமாகிப் போவதற்கு ஒப்பானது.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a simple culinary analogy to explain the role of feigned anger (புலவி) in love. Just as a moderate amount of salt (உப்பு) makes food delicious, a brief period of pouting adds flavor and excitement to a relationship. However, if the lovers prolong this disagreement (நீள விடல்), it becomes like adding too much salt (மிக்கற்றால்), which ruins the entire experience. The words 'அமைந்தற்றால்' (like being in right measure) and 'மிக்கற்றால்' (like being excessive) highlight the importance of moderation in lovers' tiffs.

ai.literal: Those who are distressed, affliction pain causing, is like, oneself, those who have sulked, without embracing, leaving.
ai.translation: Leaving those who have sulked with us without embracing them is like inflicting further painful distress upon those who are already suffering.
ai.modern: துன்பப்படுபவர்களுக்கு மேலும் துன்பத்தைத் தருவதைப் போன்றது, நம்மிடம் ஊடல் கொண்டவரைத் தழுவிக்கொள்ளாமல் அப்படியே விட்டுவிடுவது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the act of ignoring a sulking partner to inflicting more pain on someone who is already suffering. When a lover feigns anger, they are already in a state of emotional vulnerability, longing for affection. Failing to embrace and comfort them at this moment only deepens their distress. The word 'pulantārai' refers to the partner who has sulked, and 'pullā viṭal' means leaving them without an embrace, highlighting how crucial physical affection is to resolve lovers' tiffs.

ai.literal: Not comforting those who have sulked is like cutting the root of a withered creeper.
ai.translation: Failing to appease a partner who has sulked is like cutting the root of a creeper that is already withering.
ai.modern: ஊடல் கொண்டவரை சமாதானம் செய்து ஏற்றுக்கொள்ளாமல் இருப்பது, ஏற்கனவே வாடிப் போயிருக்கும் கொடியின் வேரை அறுப்பதற்கு ஒப்பானது ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid botanical metaphor to highlight the delicate nature of love-quarrels. A partner who is sulking is emotionally vulnerable, compared here to a withered creeper. Failing to comfort or appease them in a timely manner acts as a final blow, akin to cutting the very root of that struggling plant. To sustain the relationship, one must nurture it with affection rather than letting the feigned anger harden into permanent estrangement.

ai.literal: The excellent goodness of good partners, their beauty is the quality of sulking in the hearts of those with flower-like eyes.
ai.translation: To virtuous lovers, the ultimate charm is the feigned anger that arises in the hearts of their beloveds whose eyes are like flowers.
ai.modern: மலர் போன்ற கண்களை உடைய பெண்களின் நெஞ்சில் தோன்றும் ஊடலின் தன்மையே, நல்ல குணங்களை உடைய கணவர்களுக்குக் கூடுதல் அழகைத் தருவதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights how playful sulking, or feigned anger, enhances the beauty of a romantic relationship. For loving and virtuous partners, the true charm of their bond lies in the sweet, temporary sulking that arises in the hearts of their flower-eyed beloveds. Rather than causing distance, this feigned anger acts as a decorative grace that deepens their mutual affection.

ai.literal: If prolonged sulking and feigned anger are absent, love is like an overripe fruit and an extremely unripe fruit.
ai.translation: Without prolonged sulking and feigned anger, love is like fruit that is either overripe or completely unripe.
ai.modern: நீடித்த பிணக்கும் சிறிய ஊடலும் இல்லை என்றால், காதல் என்பது அழுகிப்போன பழத்தைப் போலவும், கசக்கும் பிஞ்சுக் காயைப் போலவும் ஆகிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the necessity of lovers' tiffs in keeping a relationship healthy. 'Pulavi' refers to minor, feigned anger, while 'tuni' refers to a slightly longer, deeper sulking. If these emotional variations are missing, love loses its balance and becomes unpalatable. It becomes either like 'kani' (here meaning an overripe, mushy fruit that has lost its texture) or 'karukkāy' (an extremely young, bitter, and hard unripe fruit). Just as a fruit is best when perfectly ripe, love is best when seasoned with occasional, gentle disagreements.

ai.literal: In sulking, there is a certain pain, thinking, 'Will the reunion not be delayed?'
ai.translation: There is a certain pain even in feigned anger, arising from the anxious thought: 'Will it delay our reunion?'
ai.modern: ஊடலில் ஒரு துன்பம் இருக்கிறது; 'நமது கூடல் தாமதப்படுமோ?' என்று நினைப்பதால் அது உண்டாகிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the subtle anxiety that accompanies feigned anger (ūṭal) between lovers. While sulking is meant to enhance the pleasure of love, it brings a unique distress of its own. The lover worries that this playful disagreement might prolong their separation and delay their sweet reunion. Thus, even in the midst of playful sulking, the mind is troubled by the fear of delayed intimacy.

ai.literal: Grieving what use then, 'she has suffered' that, that-which-understands lover absent when?
ai.translation: What is the use of grieving when one does not have a lover who can understand that grief?
ai.modern: துன்பப்படுவதை உணர்ந்து கொள்ளும் காதலர் இல்லாத போது, துன்பப்படுவதால் என்ன பயன்?
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine reflects on the futility of her feigned anger or sulking. She asks what the point of her distress ('நோதல்') is if her partner is not there to notice and soothe it. Feigned anger is a game of love that requires a responsive partner; without a lover who understands that she is hurting ('நொந்தார் என்று அஃது அறியும்'), her sulking becomes meaningless. The word 'வழி' here functions as 'when' or 'in the situation of', indicating the condition under which grief is useless.

ai.literal: Water too of the shade is sweet indeed; feigned anger too with those who love is sweet.
ai.translation: Just as water is sweet when it is in the shade, a lover's tiff is sweet only when it is with those who truly love us.
ai.modern: நிழலில் உள்ள நீரே குடிக்க இனியது; அதுபோல, நம்மை விரும்புபவர்களிடம் கொள்ளும் ஊடலே இன்பம் தருவதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a beautiful analogy to explain the nature of a lover's tiff (புலவி). Water is naturally refreshing, but it is exceptionally sweet and cool when drawn from the shade rather than from an open, sun-baked area. Similarly, while love itself is sweet, a minor feigned disagreement or lover's quarrel is delightful only when it occurs with a partner who truly loves and cherishes us. The word 'வீழுநர்' refers to those who love, emphasizing that the sweetness of the tiff depends entirely on the mutual affection of the partners.

ai.literal: With him who leaves my sulking to wither, my heart saying 'we will unite' is a futile desire.
ai.translation: For my heart to think, 'We will unite with him,' who simply leaves my sulking to wither away without consoling me, is a futile, helpless longing.
ai.modern: ஊடலைத் தணிக்காமல் அது தானாகவே வாடிப் போகும்படி விட்டுவிடுகின்ற காதலரோடு, 'நாம் கூடுவோம்' என்று என் நெஞ்சம் நினைப்பது வீணான ஆசையாகும்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine laments the helpless nature of her own heart. When she enters a love-quarrel (ūṭal), her lover does not try to comfort her, but instead leaves her until her anger withers (uṇaṅka) away on its own. Despite this neglect, her heart still eagerly longs to reunite with him. She describes this persistent urge of her heart to seek union as a futile, uncontrollable desire (avā).
